{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZj_EvQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDKpDY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 89, "title": "Implement pitch-independent S-DSP BRR waveform priming during KON", "body": "## Problem

KON clears the decoded waveform, but ordinary BRR decoding subsequently depends on pitch advancement. A nonterminal voice started at pitch $0000 therefore remains silent indefinitely with NON disabled; pitch $0001 retains an empty interpolation window until its first demanded nibble. Recognizing an initial terminal header independently of pitch, added by Issue #81, does not initialize an ordinary waveform.

This is the incomplete behavior prioritized by the latest assessment. It is distinct from the completed terminal-header corrections in Issues #79/#81 and live-directory correction in Issue #77. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Implement waveform priming during KON initialization independently of programmed pitch, followed by correct sample-level pitch hold/resume behavior for stable directory entries and BRR data. Deliver a hardware behavior change, independently derived tests, and its specification reconciliation.

Use these attributed hardware sources, already identified by the repository:

- [Anomie/jwdonal S-DSP documentation, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0#file-apudsp_jwdonal-txt): KON, BRR DECODING, and SOUND GENERATION, especially initialization, interpolation position, and S3/S4 ordering.
- [Fullsnes BRR samples and interpolation](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspbrrsamples): directory layout, flag meanings, decoding, and Gaussian coefficients; [ADSR/GAIN and control registers](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm#snesapudspadsrgainenvelope): KON silence and envelope behavior.
- The repository’s [Issue #81 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/docs/issue-81-validation.md#source-reconciliation) distinguishes initialization/header recognition from pitch-driven consumption. Its [Issue #79 reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/docs/issue-79-validation.md#source-reconciliation) records the documented 12-sample buffer and conflicting ENDX descriptions.

The required contract is:

1. KON initializes the selected voice from its directory start word and primes waveform data independently of ordinary pitch advancement. Initialization silence must not imply an empty waveform afterward.
2. After initialization, pitch zero holds the initialized interpolation position and waveform. Pitch changes resume from that position without restarting, skipping, or decoding samples twice.
3. Retain initial `01` zero-envelope/release behavior, continued silent BRR processing, live end-bit loop selection, sticky ENDX, and voice isolation. Priming must not fabricate a block-end event.
4. Initialization must not alter the global noise/envelope clock or introduce an artificial programmed pitch.

**Specification uncertainty:** the repository records do not reproduce the complete initialization schedule. Exact priming count, selected interpolation window, and correspondence to `Dsp::sample` calls must be reconciled from the staged specification before fixing numerical expectations. The documented buffer capacity alone does not establish that schedule. Distinguish hardware stages from the core’s sample-call convention; supersede unsupported earlier assumptions explicitly.

Scope: stable DIR/SRCN/start/loop words and RAM across initialization; independent filter-0 vectors; NON/PMON disabled for the primary startup oracle. Preserve existing NON/PMON regressions.

Non-goals: a complete DSP subcycle scheduler, live KON-delay directory/header edits, torn writes, SPC/DSP bus races, later-block physical lookahead, preceding-envelope application timing, reset retention, new filter algorithms, firmware, enhancement chips, or UI work.

## Context and reproduction

Read-only inspection baseline: `4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd`; working tree clean. No suites were rerun during planning.

- [`dsp.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs): KON replaces `Voice` with default decoded history and `key_delay: 5`. The delay branch only checks the initial terminal header. Subsequent `decode` calls occur when pitch advances integer positions.
- [`dsp_brr_end.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_brr_end.rs): `initial_header_flags_at_zero_and_low_pitch_precede_nibble_demand` explicitly expects zero BRR output for 4095 post-delay calls. Its terminal controls remain useful; its ordinary-waveform silence expectation encodes the limitation being corrected.
- [`dsp_directory.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_directory.rs) and `dsp_brr_end.rs` derive windows from demand counts with zero-filled startup history. Review affected expectations rather than preserving them as hardware authority.

Minimal discriminator: configure a stable nonterminal range-10/filter-0 block filled with nibble +4, direct GAIN 64, pitch zero, NON/PMON off, voice volumes +64/−128, master volumes +64/+64, and echo writes disabled. KON and observe beyond initialization. Current code produces zero PCM/OUTX indefinitely. An initialized constant phase-zero window independently yields decoded value 2048, Gaussian source 4098, post-envelope output 2048, stereo `(512, -1024)`, ENVX 64, and OUTX 8. Establish the applicable startup window and call boundary from the specification before using this anchor.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the resolved initialization sequence: start selection, decoded groups, interpolation window/position, silence interval, transition to normal pitch advancement, and ENDX implications. Cite exact source sections, explain disagreements, and distinguish sample-call conventions from physical timing. A documentation-only reconciliation does not complete this Issue.
- [ ] Add original public-API tests in a focused `dsp_kon_preload.rs` target. Demonstrate behavioral failures on the exact baseline above, then passes after implementation; compilation failures do not count.
- [ ] Check numerical PCM, ENVX, OUTX, and ENDX during initialization and after it at pitches $0000/$0001. Include positive/negative constant data, a nonuniform signed filter-0 sequence that distinguishes the selected window, nonterminal `00/10/11` controls, and initial `01` silence controls. Use separately derived sequences/coefficient arithmetic, without production helpers or captured emulator output.
- [ ] Test zero-pitch holds, resume at $1000, return to zero, and retrigger with a distinct start and loop. Verify no skipped/duplicated samples, premature loop selection, stale waveform reuse, fabricated ENDX, or disturbance of an independently running voice. Freeze exact numeric vectors from the reconciled schedule.
- [ ] Add an original bounded SPC700 guest using the existing firmware-free uploader and $F2/$F3 accesses. Exercise startup, hold, and resume with independently expected PCM/register records. Compare whole versus irregular `Apu::tick` partitions, including every PCM sample, DSP registers, RAM, and output ports. Record MIT authorship/provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Preserve terminal release, silent processing, live-directory, KOFF/retrigger, NON/PMON, envelope, mixing, and echo coverage. Correct affected legacy timing/window expectations only with explicit source-derived replacements; do not remove discriminators to obtain passes.
- [ ] Pass `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_kon_preload`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --locked`.
- [ ] Run the [README validation gates](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/4d904fef0b60f7204a44681221cf17eb43ad75fd/README.md#validate): reproduce/compare the original smoke fixture; build pinned assemblers; run `tools/hardware-tests.py` with ca65/ld65/spcasm and `tools/ppu-test.py` with bass; build cleared games twice; install browser dependencies, build Wasm/web, and run `npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'` from `web`. Preserve existing game sources, pins, hashes, gameplay/replay checks, and audio assertions. Use only original or explicitly licensed source-built fixtures; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update README and validation evidence with actual results, baseline discriminators, corrected earlier contracts, and remaining limitations. Passing these diagnostics establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

Inventory remains unchanged: partial—`cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`; unimplemented—`ppu-raster`, `pal`. Preserve every category’s existing scope. None becomes verified through this Issue.

Remaining voice work includes independent filter 1–3 evidence, exhaustive interpolation phases, simultaneous key/mixing combinations, live KON-delay selection, physical header/lookahead/publication timing, register/RAM races, and reset retention. Other inventory gaps remain open.

## Optional validation

Additional original filter-0 startup vectors at other pitches. Physical-device measurements may supplement evidence but are not required for merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
